protocol.author_direction: 2026-09-14 JST: omit MCMC comparisons; benchmark matched forward functions, prioritizing line-of-sight velocity dispersion accuracy and evaluation time.
protocol.scope: A fresh, bounded forward-only experiment. The Plummer cases and JAM settings are inherited from the already observed jam9-plummer-isotropic-v1 validation; this is not an unseen-model accuracy test. Freeze this protocol and runner in git before any new evaluation or timing.
protocol.observable: Surface-density-weighted LOS second moment in (km/s)^2, with no PSF, pixel averaging or measurement noise. Its square root is sigma_los for the imposed zero-mean-velocity convention, otherwise v_rms; no streaming decomposition is inferred.

coordinates.definition: r=geomspace(rmin,rmax,N); phi=2*pi*((arange(N)*azimuth_step)%1); x=r*cos(phi), y=q_projected*r*sin(phi). N is the number of sky positions, not an observed stellar sample.

protocol.jam_settings: Callable analytic potential containing JeansPy G, tracer MGE reused for fixed tracer shape, beta=0, ml=1, interp=False, spectral_derivs=True, moment=zz, sigmapsf=0, pixsize=0, distance=0.648/pi Mpc (one arcsec per pc). Recompute the projected solver on every call; do not replace its internal radial-grid heuristic.

reference.oblate: Independent analytic hypergeometric vertical pressure and its analytic radial derivative, followed by SciPy adaptive infinite LOS quadrature. Derivation is in the runner and public report; no JeansPy force or quadrature routine is used.

accuracy.report: Store signed pointwise errors, maximum relative second-moment and square-root errors, RMS relative errors, finite-positive gates, and accuracy for every timed mass normalization. Report the complete accuracy-time curve, including failures; compare ratios only within a named accuracy threshold. No post-result order/threshold selection.

timing.mass_factors: 1 + 0.01*sin(arange(10)*0.71); the first call uses factor 1. All engines recompute predictions for the same fixed mass-normalization sequence with fixed coordinates and tracer.
stages: JAM tracer MGE fitting (once per shape/resolution, reusable across N and potential parameters)
first prediction (JAX tracing, compilation and execution included)
ten warm predictions with changed mass normalization
timing.cache_policy: Clear JAX caches before each shape/N/solver/order row; keep caches for its ten calls. Coordinates and all physical parameters are dynamic JIT arguments. NumPy and JAM recompute their ordinary public forward call each time. Synchronized device-resident timing excludes separately measured result transfer.
timing.report: Retain all ten durations, median, p10 and p90. Percentiles describe within-process timing variation, not statistical confidence across hosts. Do not mix fitting, first-call and warm costs.

protocol.accounting: Charge every execution, including failed attempts, to the existing single 86400-second campaign ledger. Check the remaining balance before launch. No new ledger or automatic budget extension.
protocol.failure_rule: Preserve each attempted row, warning, exception, failed accuracy gate and resource stop. Save after each stage and repetition. A failed independent reference blocks interpretation and timing until an explicitly labeled, frozen correction; do not silently overwrite or retune.
protocol.limitations: JAM spherical alignment and JeansPy cylindrical alignment coincide in this beta=beta_z=0 subset. The potential is spherical and smooth; this does not test flattened halos, cusps, anisotropic closures or posterior accuracy. The specialized spherical JeansPy solver is measured only for q=1. Existing NFW/flattened-Zhao forward and gradient studies remain complementary evidence. No new MCMC or paper experiment is authorized by this protocol.
